mainTopic: A thief who carries a stolen purse out on שבת: when is he exempt from paying because the theft and the שבת violation happen at the same moment (קם ליה בדרבה מיניה)?
overview: The ברייתא teaches that a thief who carries a stolen purse out of a house on שבת must pay for it, but if he dragged it out, he is exempt, because the theft and the שבת violation happen at the same moment. The גמרא explains that the ברייתא follows בן עזאי, who holds that walking counts like standing, and that the dragging case was chosen to teach that dragging a medium-sized purse is a real way of carrying out. Then the גמרא asks where he dragged it to: the public domain gives a שבת violation but no theft, and his own private domain gives theft but no שבת violation. In רב אחא's version, the answer is the sides of the public domain. According to רבי אליעזר, that area counts as public for שבת but still allows acquiring. רב אשי gives another answer: he caught the purse in his hand below three טפחים. רבינא teaches a different version, in which a thief acquires even in the public domain. The two read a משנה in בבא קמא about a stolen animal in opposite ways, and each one explains the clause that seemed to go against him. Finally, the גמרא returns to our משנה's list of forbidden relatives who receive a קנס, and contrasts it with a משנה in מכות that gives these same men מלקות. The discussion of that contradiction continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not teach the contrast within the carrying case itself?
steps.stepSummary: If the 'liable' case is when he stopped to rest, the ברייתא should have taught the contrast 'stopped to rest versus stopped to fix the load', not the dragging case.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If he stopped to adjust the load on his shoulder] he would be exempt. So instead of teaching 'if he was dragging it out, he is exempt,' the ברייתא should have drawn the line inside the carrying case itself: 'When is he liable to pay? When he stopped to rest. But if he stopped to adjust it on his shoulder, he is exempt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own earlier explanation that the thief is liable to pay because he stopped to rest. If that were true, the ברייתא had a simpler contrast available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the earlier explanation, stopping to rest splits the theft (lifting) from the שבת violation, so he pays. Stopping only to fix the load does not split them, so he is exempt. If that is the idea, the ברייתא should have shown the 'exempt' side with that same case instead of switching to a new case of dragging.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching... (a challenge: why did the ברייתא word it this way?)
Let it draw the line and teach within the same case
Stopping to rest. This breaks up the act of carrying out.
Stopping only to adjust the load on the shoulder. This does not break up the act.
Dragging the object out along the ground

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt' here means exempt from PAYING for the theft, not exempt from the שבת punishment. He is exempt from paying exactly because the שבת violation, a death-penalty sin, happens at the same moment as the theft.

phrases.english: He would be exempt.
Rather than teaching: if he was dragging and going out,
dragging and going out, he is exempt,
let it distinguish and teach within the case itself:
When is this said? When he stopped to rest,
but if he stopped to adjust it on his shoulder, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי: הָיָה מְגָרֵר וְיוֹצֵא מְגָרֵר וְיוֹצֵא פָּטוּר, נִפְלוֹג וְנִיתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation (on the previous part of the daf) that the liable case is one where he stopped to rest.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא's 'liable' case is one where the thief stopped to rest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the difference depends on stopping to rest, the natural 'exempt' contrast is stopping only to fix the load. The ברייתא's choice of a dragging case shows that this explanation is not what it meant.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows בן עזאי: walking counts as standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation: the ברייתא follows בן עזאי, who holds that each step of walking counts like a stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whose view is this? It is בן עזאי, who said: someone walking is treated like someone standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'stopped to rest' explanation and gives a new reason why the carrying thief must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בן עזאי, every step counts as a pause, so the carrying out happens only with the last step into the street. The lifting, which is the theft, came earlier, so the theft and the שבת violation are separate and he pays. He does not need to have stopped to rest.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose view is used here
Someone walking is treated like someone standing still

steps.whyThisMatters: Moving to בן עזאי means no special detail like resting is needed. Any ordinary carrying out on foot separates the theft from the שבת violation.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: הָא מַנִּי — בֶּן עַזַּאי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather: whose view is this? It is בן עזאי,
who said: one who walks is like one who stands.
phrases.notes: Each step counts as a stop, so only the final step into the other domain is the carrying out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הָא מַנִּי — בֶּן עַזַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ברייתא to a specific תנא (בן עזאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thief is liable only because he stopped to rest.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to בן עזאי, ordinary walking already separates the lifting from the carrying out, so the thief pays.

steps.title: Then why not contrast walking with throwing?
steps.stepSummary: Under בן עזאי, throwing would make him exempt, so the ברייתא should have contrasted walking with throwing instead of using dragging.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about someone who throws it out? He would be exempt. So let the ברייתא draw the line within the case itself: 'When is he liable? When he walks it out. But if he throws it, he is exempt!'
steps.whatsHappening: The same kind of question as step 1 now comes back against the new בן עזאי explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he throws, the lifting starts one continuous act that ends when the object lands, so the theft and the שבת violation happen together and he is exempt from paying. Since walking versus throwing makes a neat contrast inside the same case, why did the ברייתא use dragging?

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who throws the object out
In the case of someone who walks it out

phrases.english: But one who throws, what is the law? Exempt?
Let it distinguish and teach within the case itself:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: When is this said? With one who walks,
but one who throws is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל זוֹרֵק מַאי — פָּטוּר? נִיפְלוֹג וְנִיתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'teach it within the same case' attack against the בן עזאי answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא follows בן עזאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under בן עזאי, throwing is the natural exempt case within the same scenario. So the ברייתא's choice of dragging needs an explanation.

steps.title: Dragging was needed to teach that it counts as carrying out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא chose dragging on purpose, to teach that dragging is a real way of carrying out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא needed the case of dragging it out. You might have thought that this is not a normal way of carrying out. So it teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 3: the dragging case was chosen because it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act done in an unusual way does not count as a full מלאכה. Without this ברייתא, we might think dragging is not a normal way of carrying out. Then he would not be liable for שבת, and he would have to pay for the theft. The ברייתא shows that dragging is a real הוצאה, so he is exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal way of carrying out

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows בן עזאי. It uses dragging instead of throwing because dragging teaches something new: dragging is a real way of carrying out.

phrases.english: Dragging and going out was needed for him,
for it would enter your mind to say
that this is not a normal way of carrying out.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows why the chosen case was needed (it teaches something new)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dragging is an unusual way of carrying out, so he would not be liable for שבת, and he would have to pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dragging counts as carrying out, so the theft and the שבת violation happen together and he is exempt from paying.

steps.title: What size purse are we talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which purse size is meant. Large purses are always dragged, and small ones never are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with what kind of purse? If large ones, dragging is the normal way, so there is nothing new. If small ones, dragging is not the normal way at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the answer of step 4 by asking what case the ברייתא could mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a large purse, dragging is obviously normal, so no one would think otherwise and nothing new is taught. For a small purse, dragging is clearly not normal, so he really would not be liable for שבת. Neither size fits the new teaching of step 4.

phrases.english: And with what?
phrases.notes: He means: what size purse is the ברייתא talking about?

phrases.english: If with large ones, that is its normal way.
If with small ones, that is not its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 4 by asking what size of purse is meant.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which size of purse fits the idea that dragging is a new teaching?

steps.title: A medium-sized purse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a medium-sized purse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about medium-sized ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the case is a medium-sized purse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A medium-sized purse is sometimes dragged and sometimes carried. So one might think dragging it is not normal. The ברייתא teaches that it still counts as carrying out, so he is exempt from paying.
steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: a thief drags a medium-sized purse out on שבת. This counts as carrying out, and it happens at the same moment as the theft, so he is exempt from paying.

phrases.english: Rather, with medium-sized ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a medium-sized purse, which is sometimes dragged, so the ruling that dragging counts as carrying out is a new teaching.

steps.title: Where could both sins happen at once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where he dragged the purse. Every simple location gives only one of the two sins, never both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did he take the purse out to? If he took it into the public domain, he broke שבת, but he didn't steal it yet, because you can't acquire an item by dragging it in a public place. If he took it into his own private domain, he stole it, but he didn't break שבת, because moving from one private domain to another is not forbidden carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's case. It asks where the purse was dragged, since neither obvious place gives both the שבת sin and the theft together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'exempt from paying' only works if the theft and the שבת sin happen at the exact same moment. In רשות הרבים you get the שבת sin but no acquisition. In רשות היחיד you get acquisition but no שבת sin. So the case seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Public domain, like a main street
Private domain, an enclosed private area

steps.confusionAlert: In this version of the discussion (רב אחא's, see step 12), dragging an object only makes it yours (a valid קנין) in a place that belongs to you or isn't crowded. It does not work in a busy public street, which is why the public domain gives 'no theft.' רבינא disagrees in step 13 and holds that he does acquire it in the public domain.

phrases.english: And where did he carry it out to?
If he carried it out to the public domain,
there is a Shabbat violation,
but there is no theft violation.
If he carried it out to a private domain,
there is a theft violation,
but there is no Shabbat violation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the purse's size, the גמרא now asks where it was dragged to.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the theft and the שבת sin happen together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every possible destination produces only one of the two sins, so they can never happen at the same moment.

steps.title: He dragged it to the edges of the public street
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he dragged it to צידי רשות הרבים, the side areas next to the public street.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for a case where he took it out to the sides of the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming a special in-between place: the edges of the public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The edges of a public street are partly public and partly not. The hope is that this place counts as public for שבת and still lets him acquire the purse, so both sins happen together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (narrowing the case)
The sides of the public domain, the strip next to the houses along a street

phrases.english: It is needed only
where he carried it out to the sides of the public domain.
phrases.notes: This is the strip along the houses at the edge of the street, where people don't usually walk.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאַפְּקֵיהּ לְצִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by finding a middle location.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case as an in-between location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No place could give both the שבת sin and the theft.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sides of the public domain might give both.

steps.title: Whose opinion fits the edges of the street?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If the edges count as public (רבי אליעזר), there is no theft. If they count as not public (רבנן), there is no שבת sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this? If it follows רבי אליעזר, who says the sides of the public domain are like the public domain, then there is a שבת sin but no theft! If it follows the רבנן, who say the sides are not like the public domain, then there is theft but no שבת sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 8. It shows that the edges of the street still give only one sin, whichever opinion we follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known dispute about the status of the street's edges. Each side of that dispute seems to put the edges in one category only, public or not public. So the same problem from step 7 comes right back.

keyTerms.meaning: Are similar to / have the status of

phrases.english: And according to whom?
If according to Rabbi Eliezer, who said

phrases.aramaic: צִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ —
phrases.english: the sides of the public domain are like the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: אִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת אִיכָּא, אִיסּוּר גְּנֵיבָה לֵיכָּא!
phrases.english: there is a Shabbat violation but no theft violation!
If according to the Rabbis, who say

phrases.aramaic: צִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לָאו כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ —
phrases.english: the sides of the public domain are not like the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: אִיסּוּר גְּנֵיבָה אִיכָּא, אִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת לֵיכָּא!
phrases.english: there is a theft violation but no Shabbat violation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 8 using the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he dragged it to the sides of the public domain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under either opinion the sides fall into only one category, so you still can't get both sins together.

steps.title: The edges are public for שבת but still allow acquiring
steps.stepSummary: The answer follows רבי אליעזר. The edges count as public for שבת, because crowds sometimes spill over there. They still allow acquiring, because people aren't usually there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it follows רבי אליעזר. When רבי אליעזר said the sides of the public domain are like the public domain, he meant only for being liable on שבת, because sometimes crowds push and go in there. But for acquiring, a person does acquire there. Why? Because the public isn't usually there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. It explains that רבי אליעזר's rule applies only to שבת, not to acquiring property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same place can have two different statuses for two different laws. For שבת, what matters is that crowds sometimes use it, so it counts as public. For acquiring, what matters is that crowds usually aren't there, so dragging works. So both sins really do happen at the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (holding on to the original idea)
The public is not usually found there

steps.whatToRemember: One location can count as public for שבת and still not count as public for acquiring. That is how the ברייתא's case works: the theft and the שבת sin happen together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: one place or thing can have a different status depending on which law we are asking about.

phrases.english: Really, it is according to Rabbi Eliezer,
and when Rabbi Eliezer said

phrases.aramaic: צִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ —
phrases.english: the sides of the public domain are like the public domain,
that applies only to being liable for Shabbat,
since sometimes the crowds push and go in there.
But for acquiring, he does acquire.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא — דְּהָא לָא שְׁכִיחִי רַבִּים.
phrases.english: What is the reason? Because the public is not usually found there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by limiting רבי אליעזר's rule to שבת only.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a rule to one area of law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי אליעזר, the sides count as public for everything, so there is no acquiring there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sides count as public only for שבת. Dragging still acquires there, since crowds usually aren't present.

steps.title: רב אשי: he caught it in his hand near the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. He lowered his hand below three טפחים and caught the purse in it. That counts as putting it down for שבת, and his hand acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The case is where he brought his hand down below three טפחים and caught the purse. This follows רבא, who said: A person's hand counts for him like a space of four by four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another way the theft and the שבת sin can happen together, even in the public domain itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His hand is near the ground and counts as a proper 4x4 surface, so the purse is considered 'put down' there for שבת. His hand also belongs to him, so the purse becomes his at that same moment. This gives both sins at once without needing the edges of the street.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought his hand together (under the purse)
Below three טפחים from the ground
Four by four טפחים, the minimum size of a 'place' for שבת carrying

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
For example, where he brought his hand
below three handbreadths and received it.
phrases.notes: Below three טפחים from the ground counts like the ground itself, so the purse has been 'put down' in the street.

phrases.english: This is like Rava.
As Rava said:
A person's hand is considered for him
like four by four handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁצֵּירַף יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the problem of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case definition using his hand as the place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sins can only come together at the edges of the public street.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in the public street, catching the purse in his hand near the ground gives both sins at once.

steps.title: This is how רב אחא taught it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this whole discussion is the version that רב אחא taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא taught it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short note about who taught this version of the discussion. It sets up the next move: רבינא's different version comes in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase tells us that what we just learned is how רב אחא passed it down. A line like this often comes right before another teacher's different version.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa taught it this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names who taught the discussion that came before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The preceding discussion is רב אחא's version of the sugya.

steps.title: רבינא's version: the public domain also acquires
steps.stepSummary: רבינא teaches the case differently. The thief carried the purse into רשות הרבים, and he acquires it right there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא taught: Really, he carried it out to the public domain, and in the public domain he also acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבינא's version of the whole discussion, which competes with רב אחא's version. In רבינא's view, a thief acquires an object as soon as he takes it out of the owner's domain, even into the public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אחא's version, the thief only acquired the purse once it came into his own domain, so the גמרא needed the edge areas or the low hand. רבינא says removing the purse to רשות הרבים already makes it stolen. So the theft and the שבת sin happen at the same moment, and the simple case works with no special setup.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (the simple case after all)
he acquired it (became responsible as owner/thief)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new step in רב אחא's discussion. It is a separate, competing version of the whole sugya, so the earlier answers about the edges and the hand are not needed here.

phrases.english: Ravina taught it this way:
Really, he carried it out to the public domain,
phrases.notes: "It" is the stolen purse from the earlier case, taken on שבת.

phrases.english: and in the public domain he also acquires it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a rival version of the discussion that step 12 credited to רב אחא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the acquisition rule so the original question has a simple answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A thief only acquires once the object reaches his own domain (רב אחא).
steps.terutzMaskana: Taking the object out of the owner's domain, even into רשות הרבים, already acquires it.

steps.title: Both readings come from one משנה about a stolen animal
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא are arguing over how to read a משנה about a thief who pulls an animal out and it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the two of them disagree about what to infer from this mishna, as we learned: If he was pulling it and going out, and it died in the owner's domain, he is exempt. If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's domain and it died, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the source that both אמוראים read differently. Next it will show how each one draws his view from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two clauses. If the animal dies while still in the owner's domain, the thief is exempt. If he lifted it or took it out, he is liable. What "took it out" means is the open question: out to anywhere, or into his own domain?

keyTerms.meaning: an inference read out of the exact wording
he lifted it (a way of acquiring)

phrases.english: And the two of them, about the inference
of this mishna, disagree.
As we learned:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא קמא, about someone who steals an animal.

phrases.english: If he was pulling it and going out
and it died in the owner's domain, he is exempt.
If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's domain
and it died, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the source behind the disagreement between the versions of רב אחא and רבינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief is exempt if the animal dies in the owner's domain, and liable if he lifted it or took it out.

steps.title: רבינא reads the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רבינא infers from the רישא that once the animal is out of the owner's domain, the thief is liable, even if it is not in his own domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא infers from the first clause, and רב אחא infers from the last clause. רבינא infers from the first clause: If he was pulling it and going out, and it died in the owner's domain, he is exempt. The reason is that it died in the owner's domain. But if he took it out of the owner's domain and it died, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first says each אמורא leans on a different clause, then shows רבינא's reading of the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause exempts the thief only because the animal died "in the owner's domain." So if it was already outside the owner's domain, anywhere at all, he is liable. That means leaving the owner's domain is enough to acquire it, which is רבינא's view.

phrases.english: Ravina infers from the first clause,
Rav Acha infers from the last clause.
Ravina infers from the first clause:
If he was pulling it and going out
and it died in the owner's domain, he is exempt.
The reason is that it died in the owner's domain;
but if he took it out of the owner's domain and it died
he is liable.
phrases.notes: Even if it only reached the public street and not his own property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבינא draws his view from the first clause of the משנה cited in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's view that removing the object to רשות הרבים already acquires it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first clause of the בבא קמא משנה, which exempts only when the animal dies in the owner's domain

steps.title: רב אחא reads the last clause
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא compares taking out to lifting. Lifting brings the animal into the thief's domain, so taking out must mean bringing it into his domain too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא infers from the last clause: "He lifted it or took it out." Taking out is like lifting. Just as lifting means it comes into his domain, so too taking out means it comes into his domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רב אחא's reading of the second clause, which supports his view that the object must come into the thief's own domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts "lifted" and "took out" side by side, so they should work the same way. Lifting puts the animal in the thief's own hands. So "took out" must also mean he brought it into his own domain, not just into the street.

phrases.english: Rav Acha infers from the last clause:
"He lifted it or took it out."
Taking out is like lifting:
Just as lifting is where it comes into his domain,
so too taking out is where it comes into his domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading, from the other clause of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא's view that the thief acquires only when the object comes into his own domain
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last clause of the בבא קמא משנה, where taking out is paired with lifting

steps.title: Each reading has trouble with the other clause
steps.stepSummary: The first clause seems to go against רב אחא, and the last clause seems to go against רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב אחא the first clause is difficult, and for רבינא the last clause is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that each אמורא's reading clashes with the clause the other one relies on. It will answer each problem next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's reading of the רישא implies that leaving the owner's domain is enough, which goes against רב אחא. רב אחא's reading of the סיפא implies that the animal must reach the thief's domain, which goes against רבינא.

phrases.english: For Rav Acha, the first clause is difficult,
for Ravina, the last clause is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב אַחָא קַשְׁיָא רֵישָׁא, לְרָבִינָא קַשְׁיָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses each inference against the other אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both readings of the בבא קמא משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each clause, read closely, seems to support one אמורא and contradict the other, so neither can explain the whole משנה.

steps.title: רב אחא explains the first clause
steps.stepSummary: For רב אחא, until the animal reaches the thief's domain, it still counts as the owner's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is not difficult for רב אחא: As long as it has not come into his domain, we call it the owner's domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem against רב אחא by widening what "the owner's domain" means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא reads "died in the owner's domain" to include the public street. As long as the thief has not brought the animal into his own domain, legally it is still under the owner. So the first clause fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: as long as it has not
we call it, we apply the term to it

phrases.english: The first clause is not difficult for Rav Acha:
as long as it has not come into his domain,
we call it the owner's domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines a term in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "The owner's domain" means only the owner's actual property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Anywhere outside the thief's domain still counts as "the owner's domain."

steps.title: רבינא explains the last clause
steps.stepSummary: רבינא does not accept that taking out must be compared to lifting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause is not difficult for רבינא: We do not say that taking out is like lifting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem against רבינא by rejecting the comparison that רב אחא relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבינא, lifting and taking out are two separate ways to acquire, even though they are listed together. Taking out works just by leaving the owner's domain, so the last clause does not need the animal to reach the thief's own domain.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not say, we do not accept this

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא says a thief acquires once the object leaves the owner's domain. רב אחא says it must come into the thief's own domain. Each reads one clause of the same משנה, and each can explain the other clause.

phrases.english: The last clause is not difficult for Ravina:
we do not say that taking out is like lifting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the challenge in step 17 and closes this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the comparison behind the inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since taking out is listed with lifting, it must also mean reaching the thief's domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two are not compared, so taking out works once the animal leaves the owner's domain.

steps.title: Back to our משנה: one who is with his sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the list in our משנה of forbidden relatives for whom a קנס is paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: "One who has relations with his sister, or with his father's sister, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of our משנה to begin a new discussion. It is setting up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה listed girls from forbidden relationships, like a sister or an aunt, and said the man still pays the girl's קנס. The גמרא now wants to check this against another משנה.

phrases.english: One who has relations with his sister
or with his father's sister, etc.
phrases.notes: Our משנה continues the list and says a fine is paid for these girls.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the theft discussion and returns to the text of our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה says a קנס is paid even for a girl who is a forbidden relative.

steps.title: A משנה in מכות says these men get lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in מכות that lists the same relationships as cases of מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with this: These are the ones who receive lashes: one who has relations with his sister, or with his father's sister, or with his mother's sister, or with his wife's sister, or with his brother's wife, or with his father's brother's wife, or with a menstruating woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a contradiction by quoting the משנה in מכות. It will spell out exactly what the problem is next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the man pays a קנס for these women. The משנה in מכות says the same man gets מלקות for the very same acts. The גמרא is lining up the two so it can ask how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: and they contrasted it (raised a contradiction)
a woman in her menstrual state

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
These are the ones who receive lashes:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מכות.

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו,
phrases.english: one who has relations with his sister, or with his father's sister,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: or with his mother's sister, or with his wife's sister,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו, וְעַל אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אָבִיו,
phrases.english: or with his brother's wife, or with his father's brother's wife,
or with a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets another משנה against the line of our משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's ruling that a קנס is paid for these forbidden relatives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in מכות gives the same man מלקות for the same acts. The גמרא is setting up the question of how he can both get lashes and pay the fine.
